title: The layered CHORDS stack read as saw-toothy and went 'pop pop' on every chord — two saws doing one job, plus a gated noise burst

ownerWords: it just sounds a bit saw-toothy or something? Like almost mechanical/electronic... less lush and organic like I'd like chords
it's like the layered one goes 'pop' 'pop' with two hits whenever a chord goes. Which just seems odd? ... its sort of like a percussive hit.
It has a layer of noise that I'd probably want to try to make a bit cleaner. It also sounds almost like there's a snare hit or percussion hit whenever the chord comes in

measured.note: Each before/after pair was rendered from the same figure, key and tempo and loudness-normalized TOGETHER in one vary batch, so these deltas are the treatment and not gain. 'harsh 1.6-3.8 kHz %' is the share of total spectral energy in the band docs/priors/layering.md §1/§3 names as the metallic-harshness band — the band the de-harsh EQ pair exists to cut, and the band the owner's word 'saw-toothy' points at.

cause.sawToothy: The pad and the stab were both sawtooth, both at transpose 0, both highpassed within 30-80 Hz of each other, and NEITHER was lowpassed at all. docs/priors/organic-vs-mechanical.md §4d measured 3,559 professional patches and found chord patches are the most heavily lowpassed role there is (82.1%, median knob 523 Hz); a raw saw pair is outside the middle of that distribution by a wide margin. §4c adds that chord patches waveshape at 14.3% against bass's 62.8%, and dotbeat was driving every layer of every role identically.
cause.popPop: Two short percussive events per chord. (a) The stab: 2 ms attack, gated to one or two 16th notes under a chord that sustains — a chop, not a chord. 131 P2 measured pack chords attacking in ~7 ms, so 2 ms was five times faster than the reference class. (b) The air layer: 30-65% noise, 4 ms attack, gated to 3 steps, highpassed 2-3.5 kHz — that is the construction of a clap, fired on every chord onset.
cause.fuseAttacksDidNotCatchIt: The helper written for exactly this excluded the bottom lowpassed layer from its onset-forming set, so a 2-layer body+stab draw (which is what seed 2156 is) had one member and the function returned early. It also clamped non-onset-forming layers, i.e. it rewrote a 200 ms pad swell to a 27 ms attack, manufacturing a second pluck.
cause.andItWasDry: Every layer's reverb/delay send was being zeroed by a rule that pinned sends to 0 on every mono layer — conflating mono discipline with dry discipline. Fixed one commit earlier on the same branch; measured here at a return sitting 21.5 dB under the mix on case-22, against 18.5 dB for the engineplus arm the owner said had the ambience he liked.

whyThisPairMatters: research/122 §8 and research/123 §6 both call a matched before/after pair the single most valuable asset in the taste program, because the roughness signal only exists BETWEEN matched renders of the same material — commercial reference loops score 77% above the owner's own fail clip on Daniel-Weber, so no absolute threshold can work. Before this case the bank held n=1 such pair (case-19/20). It now holds n=3, which is the threshold every 'soft until n>=3 pairs' comment in the codebase is waiting on — though two of the three are the same defect family and only one is owner-confirmed on BOTH sides, so treat n=3 as a floor reached, not a calibration earned.
